subject: Life Skills
title: Time Blocking
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Time Blocking.

hook.text: Cal Newport schedules every minute of his day into blocks. He publishes five books, teaches, and raises a family.

buildup.text: A to-do list tells you what needs doing. A time block tells you when you will do it. The 'when' is what matters.

discovery.text: Assign each task a specific block on your calendar. When the block starts, that task is the only thing you do.

twist.text: Plans will break. The point is not perfection. It is intention. A broken plan still beats no plan at all.

climax.text: Review and adjust blocks twice a day — once at lunch, once in late afternoon. Flexibility inside structure works best.

punchline.text: A schedule is a promise to yourself. Keep most of them.

quiz.question: What is the point of time blocking if plans often change?
options: It creates rigid discipline that prevents flexibility
It forces intention about what and when, even if adjusted later
It only works for people with predictable schedules
